Read the text and answer.
Night trains were once considered outdated, replaced by cheap flights and fast motorways. Yet several European railway companies are now investing in new sleeper services. Supporters argue that travelling overnight saves a hotel bill and a day of work, and that a train journey produces far less carbon dioxide than a flight of the same distance. Critics, however, point out that tickets for sleeper compartments are often more expensive than airline tickets, and that building new carriages is slow because only a few factories in Europe still make them. A recent survey found that 38 per cent of young travellers would choose a night train if the price were comparable to a flight. Several governments have therefore started to subsidise routes that cross national borders.

Why do supporters favour night trains?
They are cheaper than all flights.
They save money, time and emissions.
